open_obligations: Check that the three phases described match the setup defined in Burns et al. (2023)
Note that the weak supervisor sees strong-model debate transcripts, so it is no longer purely weak; check whether this changes how PGR should be compared with Burns et al.

Note that the from-record's paper trains an ensemble of weak models on debate arguments, while in Burns et al.'s setup the weak supervisor is a small pretrained model finetuned on ground truth labels; check how this affects the comparison with Burns et al.'s results.

Note that the from-record's paper says that in its experimental settings the gaps in compute between weak and strong models (Qwen-7B and Qwen-14B) are not significantly large, which may limit their performances, whereas Burns et al. pose the weak-to-strong learning problem as how a weak supervisor can oversee a model much smarter than it.

text: The authors say the weak-to-strong pipeline in Burns et al. (2023), also adopted in subsequent work, usually consists of three phases, the first of which creates the weak supervisor by fine-tuning a small pretrained model on ground-truth labels. In this study, they build the strong student model following three steps: (1) generate arguments from a debate between two instances of a large pretrained model; (2) train an ensemble of weak models using these debate arguments; and (3) a further training step, whose description is cut off in the cited passage.
title: Burns et al.'s three-phase setup and the authors' three-step build of the strong student
